title: Integrate Playwright CLI (@playwright/cli) as the agent browser-verification lane
description:
Why: several review findings are PARTIAL because no reviewer could drive a browser: trust-chain pause reset (h1-opus-F1), mobile nav close (h1-opus-F14), dead anchors (h1-opus-F2), missing h1 (h1-opus-F3), and header hit areas (l2-luna-F2). Playwright CLI (`@playwright/cli`) is Microsoft's token-efficient browser CLI for coding agents. It works through skills instead of MCP tool schemas (README, "Playwright CLI vs Playwright MCP"). Agents can use it to verify these fixes cheaply against `astro preview`.

Scope:
1. Install. Pin an exact `@playwright/cli` version, as a devDependency or a documented global install; never `@latest` in committed config. Match the Playwright browser build the test runner uses.
2. Config at `.playwright/cli.config.json` (the CLI's default path):
   - `browser.isolated: true` keeps the profile in memory. AGENTS.md forbids persistent or real browser profiles.
   - `browserName: chromium` and `codegen: "typescript"`.
   - `outputDir` under `.build/reports/playwright-cli/`, so the BUILD SSoT owns the path. Add a build.config.json key if one is needed.
   - `outputMode: "file"`.
   - `network.allowedOrigins` limited to the local preview origin plus the font and CDN hosts the pages need.
3. Skills. Run `playwright-cli install --skills` and review the generated files before committing. Keep `.agents/AGENT_MANIFEST.yaml` and tests/lint-agent-manifest-skills-sync.test.mts in sync.
4. Docs. In the AGENTS.md MCP section, say when to use each lane:
   - playwright-cli for agent verification and for generating new specs;
   - the playwright MCP server for exploratory or long-running work;
   - the Playwright test runner for CI.
   Decide whether the playwright MCP entry in .mcp.json / .codex/config.toml stays, and change it only through sync-mcp.sh.
5. Gitignore any session output the CLI writes outside outputDir.
6. Use it. Verify the fixes for the findings above with `playwright-cli open http://localhost:4321/...`, `snapshot`, `click`, and `screenshot`, and record the evidence in those beads.

Acceptance:
- `playwright-cli --version` reports the pinned version after a clean install.
- The config is isolated (no persistent profile) and writes only under `.build/reports/`.
- AGENTS.md documents the three Playwright lanes, and the path-citation and manifest lint tests pass.
- At least one review finding is verified end to end with playwright-cli against `astro preview`.

title: l1-astra-F1: Logo conversion recursively deletes a caller-owned temporary directory
description:
- severity: Critical
- category: bug
- location: scripts/convert-logos.sh:21, scripts/convert-logos.sh:32, scripts/convert-logos.sh:160
- evidence: SUPPORTED — read the complete script. `TEMP_DIR` accepts an existing directory, `mkdir -p` does not establish ownership, and successful completion unconditionally removes that entire directory. No deletion was executed.

```diff
-TEMP_DIR=${TEMP_DIR:-tmp/logo-conversion}
+TEMP_ROOT=${TEMP_DIR:-.build/cache/logo-conversion}
@@
-mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR" "$TEMP_DIR"
+mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR" "$TEMP_ROOT"
+TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d "$TEMP_ROOT/run.XXXXXX")
+trap 'rm -rf -- "$TEMP_DIR"' EXIT
@@
-# Cleanup
-rm -rf "$TEMP_DIR"
+# The EXIT trap removes only this run's temporary directory.
```

description:

- evidence: SUPPORTED — read the full component. The effect runs on every `paused` change and calls `setStep(0)` before it checks `paused`, so every hover or focus wipes the chain. Not reproduced in a browser: Playwright cannot catch it because `navigator.webdriver` skips the animation (56-66).

Pausing then freezes the chain and does not reset it.

description:

- scenario: Three independent breaks stack:
  1. No `*-linux.png` baseline is tracked for any suite. On every PR the compare-only step (playwright.yml:252-257) therefore fails every snapshot assertion with "snapshot doesn't exist" and `continue-on-error: true` hides it. The comment at playwright.yml:235-240 justifies `continue-on-error` by selector drift, not by missing baselines.
  2. The only documented regeneration path (`workflow_dispatch` → `--update-snapshots` → commit, playwright.yml:259-277) runs `git add tests/**/*-snapshots/ 2>/dev/null || true`. The default Actions shell is `bash` without `globstar`, so the shell passes the literal string; git's default pathspec matcher requires a full-path match and `tests/**/*-snapshots/` never matches `tests/<x>.spec.ts-snapshots/<file>.png` (the `ls-files` probe above uses the same matcher and lists zero files). `git diff --staged --quiet` then sees nothing, nothing is committed, and `git push || true` swallows whatever is left. Baselines can never land through CI.
  3. `.gitignore:42-45` ignores host-specific PNGs for `styling-snapshots` and `device-tour` only; `vision-page.spec.ts-snapshots/` has no rule, so four macOS PNGs are committed, contradicting AGENTS.md:335 ("Only Linux-pinned PNGs are committed"). - fix: (a) Replace the pathspec with one git matches, e.g. `git add -- 'tests/*-snapshots/*-linux.png'`, and drop `|| true` on `git push` so failures surface. (b) Add `tests/vision-page.spec.ts-snapshots/*.png` + `!…/*-linux.png` to .gitignore and `git rm --cached` the four darwin PNGs. (c) Trigger one `workflow_dispatch` to seed chromium baselines; until then run compare-only with `--project=chromium` only. (d) Once baselines exist, remove `continue-on-error`. Also add `timeout-minutes` to this job (none today; the `test` job has 20).

title: h2-fable-F4: SRI on the stable-URL `/assets/theme.css` is the stale-HTML break; the `pt449` purge mitigates only the...
description:

- location: scripts/sri.mjs:13,31-45; src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro:104; .github/workflows/deploy.yml:41-106
- evidence: PARTIAL — code read in full; production cache behaviour (whether Cloudflare actually caches HTML, GitHub Pages CDN propagation delay) is unobservable from here.
- scenario: `sri.mjs` skips every external URL (`isHttp`) and stamps `integrity` on every same-origin `<script src>` / `<link rel=stylesheet>` it can read from `.build/dist`. `BaseLayout.astro:104` links `/assets/theme.css`, a `public/` file whose URL never changes while its bytes change on most deploys. Same-origin SRI adds no security against an attacker who can already serve your HTML, so the fragility buys nothing.
- fix: Smallest change: in `sri.mjs` skip assets outside `/_astro/` (content-hashed) — i.e. `if (!local.startsWith("_astro/")) continue;` — so stable-URL `public/` assets carry no `integrity`. The structural fix (HTML `max-age=0, must-revalidate`, hashed assets `immutable`) is already specified in `openspec/changes/migrate-deploy-to-cloudflare-pages/proposal.md:20-24`; this finding should be cross-referenced there so the purge step is retired at cutover rather than carried forward.

title: h3-sol-F1: Codex's environment-file guard reads the wrong input and uses an unsupported denial
description:
- severity: Major
- category: security
- location: .codex/hooks.json:5-9; .codex/hooks.json:16-20; .claude/settings.json:33-37
- evidence: SUPPORTED — read both complete hook configurations. Executing the exact Codex pre-hook with a synthetic `apply_patch` envelope containing an `.env` update returned exit 0, no denial JSON, no stderr. No patch was applied. Current [Codex hook documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks#pretooluse) says patch input is `tool_input.command`; `Edit`/`Write` are valid matcher aliases, but `continue: false` and `stopReason` are unsupported denial fields.
- scenario: a normal Codex edit to `.env` reaches the hook, which extracts absent `file_path` as `null` and permits it. Even an envelope containing `file_path` produces the unsupported Claude-style response and exit 1. The post-hook has the same input mismatch and passes `null` as the formatter target. Separately, the shared shell guard returns exit 0 on malformed JSON; its Claude registration covers only Write/Edit, leaving other write mechanisms outside this particular guard. Actual client hook registration and user-level restrictions were not exercised.
- fix: adapt the Codex hooks to command/patch input, inspect every affected path, and emit `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: "deny"` or exit 2. Fail closed on malformed protected-operation input. Derive post-hook file targets from the actual patch envelope. Keep Claude and Codex response protocols separate.
- effort: M

A control containing `tool_input.file_path: ".env"` returned exit 1 and the legacy denial object; malformed JSON returned exit 0 despite a jq parse error. No edit or formatter ran. Thus changing the matcher alone would not fix it. AGENTS.md's protection of secrets does not repair the executable guard; no applicable OpenSpec exemption was found. This confirms a broken hook, not bypass of every client permission boundary.
- fix check: correct — parse all affected patch paths, including moves, reject malformed matched input, use Codex's supported denial response or exit 2, and derive post-hook targets from the patch; retain the distinct Claude protocol.

title: h3-sol-F3: Snapshot comparison executes PR code with a repository-write credential
description:
- severity: Major
- category: security
- location: .github/workflows/playwright.yml:194-220; .github/workflows/playwright.yml:222-277
- evidence: PARTIAL — source grants the entire visual-regression job `contents: write`, checks out PR code without disabling credential persistence, and runs its dependency installation, build, and tests. Only the final snapshot-update/push steps are dispatch-gated. [GitHub's permissions documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/workflow-syntax-for-github-actions) confirms that job permissions apply to all its commands/actions; [checkout documentation](https://github.com/actions/checkout#usage) documents persisted authentication by default. Effective organization/repository policy was not inspected.
- scenario: a compromised install/build/test process on a same-repository PR can use the job's write capability before the guarded commit step. A conditional around the intended push does not constrain other commands. Ordinary fork PRs receive a downgraded read-only token by default, so this is not an established fork-to-write escalation.
- fix: separate read-only PR comparison from the dispatch-only snapshot-update job; grant write permission only to the latter. Disable checkout credential persistence where authenticated Git writes are unnecessary.
- effort: M

Install, build, and comparison execute in that job before the dispatch-only update/commit guards. The comment at lines 194-198 expressly intends to leave write capability available during PR runs, but a step condition cannot restrict a compromised earlier process. The [checkout README at the exact pinned commit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/actions/checkout/de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd/README.md) confirms that v6 moves credential storage while preserving authenticated Git operations by default; the storage change therefore does not refute the concern. The intended manual snapshot-update workflow explains the grant but does not require granting it to comparison runs. Organization restrictions, branch protection, actual runner credentials, and an authenticated write were not inspected or exercised, so an exploitable repository-write path is not CONFIRMED.

description:

- category: test

Use it before the first interaction in every TrustChainIsland touch, keyboard, and click test. Do not change the hydration directive. Verify on Mobile Safari, Mobile Safari (iPhone 14 Pro Max), and Tablet Safari in the CI image.

title: Playwright specs flake under host load: networkidle, Google Fonts on page load, and a 5 s hydration wait
description:
- severity: Minor (CI flake risk under load)
- category: test
- location: tests/home.spec.ts:490 (`waitForLoadState("networkidle")`); tests/footer.spec.ts:85 (`page.goto("/")` waits for load, which blocks on the render-blocking Google Fonts stylesheet); tests/helpers/trust-chain-hydration.ts:9 (hydration wait with the default 5 s expect timeout)
- evidence: SUPPORTED. In the CI image on 2590621, a run that shared the host with the full local Chromium suite had 3 failures:
  - firefox home.spec:486 timed out at networkidle;
  - webkit footer.spec:82 timed out at goto;
  - Mobile Safari (iPhone 14 Pro Max) home.spec:153: the island still had `ssr` after 5 s.
  The same tree run alone passed 290/0, and so did 74cac5c.
- scenario: a loaded GitHub runner (5 shards in parallel), or a slow fonts.googleapis.com fetch, turns these into intermittent red runs.
- fix:
  - Replace `networkidle` waits with state-based waits (a specific locator or hydration).
  - Stop depending on the third-party font fetch for page load in tests: route fonts.googleapis.com and gstatic to local fixtures, or wait for `domcontentloaded` where the load event is irrelevant.
  - Give the hydration helper an explicit, documented timeout that matches the slowest supported project.
  - Verify by running the WebKit and Firefox projects in the CI image alongside a parallel load.
